messages:
oncall-bot: PAGE: High p95 latency detected for /v1/generate in us-west1. service=inference-runtime p50=320ms p95=1.8s (baseline p95=450ms). severity=high. incident=INC-4234509123. auto-escalation to #incidents.
sre-ashok: ack — I'm on it. grabbing traces and checking host perf counters now. @infra-alex @eng-kate please standby.
support-lina: any visible customer errors yet? CS reporting timeouts from one enterprise tenant in us-west.
prod-jordan: customer-impact: several customers seeing elevated client retries and a few API timeouts (5xx from gateway). I flagged top 3 customers, reaching out to CS for exact counts.
eng-kate: looking at service traces — p95 spike correlates with long kernel scheduling spans on a subset of hosts. pulling `perf top` and `perf record` now. command I'll run: `sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 20` then `perf script`.
eng-ron: grabbing Jaeger spans for a sample request id: `trace=8f3b2a` — long span inside `runtime/infer_loop` between `kv_cache.fetch` and `attention.forward`. attaching short span:
```
span: runtime/infer_loop (1200ms)
  child: kv_cache.fetch (700ms)
  child: attention.forward (400ms)
```
this matches host-level preemption in perf samples.
infra-alex: rolling host list shows a kernel update (6.1.12 -> 6.1.14) rolled to a canary pool ~12h ago and then to more hosts ~3h ago. correlates with first p95 uptick in metrics around 2.5h ago.
sre-ashok: hypothesis A: kernel scheduler change introduced regressions under our workload causing longer runqueue latencies. Hypothesis B: increased batched request size triggered a codepath regression in attention kernel. need perf counters (context-switches, runqueue length) + cpu steal.
eng-kate: collecting `dstat` and `vmstat` dumps from affected hosts and uploading to GCS: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-4234509123/
support-lina: CS confirms 9 affected customers, 2 hit their client-side retry limit and reported degraded UX. tagging impacted accounts: acct-42, acct-77.
prod-jordan: drafting customer status: "We're investigating elevated inference latency in us-west. We're mitigating and will share ETA within 30m. No data loss."
eng-ron: quick mitigation idea: enable model-fallback routing to smaller quantized variant for traffic from affected region. I can flip a routing rule for canary traffic — low risk. thoughts?
infra-alex: immediate mitigation: scale out inference pool by +25% in us-west and enable fallback routing. starting scale now.
sre-ashok: mitigation steps executed: scaled +20% (inflight), enabled fallback for route /v1/generate (model: redwood/tiny-quant) for 15% of traffic. early telemetry shows p95 down to 1.1s from 1.8s for routed traffic.
eng-kate: still seeing heavy KV fetch spans on some hosts. pushing `perf record` outputs and sample stack traces to incident folder. sample stack excerpt:
```
#0  __schedule
#1  schedule
#2  __mutex_lock_slowpath
#3  kv_cache_lock
#4  kv_cache.fetch
#5  runtime/infer_loop
```
eng-ron: trace correlation: high tail time aligns with hosts with higher rq-sz and `nr_running` spikes. attaching heatmap in the doc.
prod-jordan: customer notification sent to affected accounts with the mitigation note and link to status page. CS will follow up.
sre-ashok: running next steps checklist: (1) continue perf capture (2) collect kernel boot logs for affected hosts (3) check recent kernel git/logs for scheduler patches (4) prepare rollback plan for kernel if needed.
infra-alex: rollback plan ready: if we see sig decrease in throughput after kernel rollback test on canary, we will rollback 6.1.14 -> 6.1.12 on affected hosts. need eng signoff for risk assessment.
eng-kate: quick local repro attempt: running microbench that simulates KV cache contention reproduced increased tail under new kernel; sharing script in the incident folder.
sre-ashok: timeline notes so far:
  - 4234470000 ~ canary kernel 6.1.14 deployed to small pool
  - 4234492000 ~ first p95 uptick detected in metrics
  - 4234509123 ~ oncall-bot page triggered (root)
  - 4234510000 ~ mitigation scale + fallback enabled
  - 4234510200 ~ partial improvement observed for routed traffic
please add any new events to the doc.
eng-ron: next diagnostic: capture perf counters for `context-switches` and `cpu-migrations` and attach `trace-cmd` output.
support-lina: are we set to send a public status update? I can post to status.redwood if prod approves.
prod-jordan: yes, send a brief status: "Mitigations in place — traffic routed to fallback model and pool scaled. Investigating kernel scheduling regression as a possible cause. No data loss."
sre-ashok: assigning RCA owners: eng-kate (perf analysis), eng-ron (traces + microbench), infra-alex (kernel rollout & rollback), prod-jordan (customer comms). handing off to the morning oncall at 4234580000. please keep the incident doc updated. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: channel archived to #incidents after handoff. Link to runbook: /runbooks/p95-regression.
prod-jordan: final note before handoff — please capture 1) representative perf script for each host, 2) trace ids for top 5 slow requests, 3) exact list of rolled kernel commits. Will pick up on next shift.
eng-kate: done uploading artifacts. GCS path: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-4234509123/artifacts/ — contains perf.data, traces.json, microbench outputs.
eng-ron: leaving a pointer to the hypothesis tracker doc: https://internal.redwood/hypotheses/INC-4234509123 (please don't publicize)
sre-ashok: handing off to morning oncall @sre-morning. all — if anything changes ping me directly.
